This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

The chords play the 3-2 son clave over two bars. First bar (shown): 1, the and of 2, 4. Second bar: 2 and 3. Faith, Desire, I Want Candy.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: 3+3+2 (tresillo)

Start with something simpler. Three held chords in a bar of eight eighth notes, grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Clocks, Shape of You, Eye of the Tiger.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-tresillo.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: 3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars: the tresillo (1, the and of 2, 4) in the first, then 2 and 3 in the second. That is the 3-2 son clave. Clap it before you play it.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}},{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo) (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [3+3+2 (tresillo)](chords-tresillo.qmd).
- **Leads to:** [The Barbara Ann rhythm](chords-barbara.qmd), [Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2](chords-g333322.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Son clave (3-2)](drums-clave32.qmd) (drum groove), [Bo Diddley beat](drums-bodiddley.qmd) (drum groove), [Son clave (2-3)](drums-clave.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in straight-eighth rock:** [Root eighths](bass-eighths.qmd) (bass line), [Rock backbeat](drums-rock.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords-oompah.qmd), [Waltz in one](chords-waltz.qmd), [Ballad: rocking](chords-ball-rock.qmd), [Ballad: half-broken](chords-ball-broken.qmd), [Ballad: syncopated](chords-ball-sync.qmd), [Quarter-note chords](chords-quarters.qmd), [Triplet chords (12/8)](chords-triplets.qmd), [Driving eighths](chords-eighths.qmd).
